Some problems can have more than one answer. (g): red, green, red × 9 = purple, brown, purple, brown. (h): red, green, purple × purple = 5,999. (i): red, green, purple × green = 2,000.
items.reason: The task is to fill the coloured boxes; the LP gives 202 × 9 = 1,818 and 857 × 7 = 5,999 and says (i) has no answer, so the figure fills (g) and (h) in ANSWER and marks (i) as impossible.

diagram.manim_description: On a 1920 by 1080 white canvas (BG) draw three vertical-multiplication frames side by side, left to right, 100 px apart, the whole group centred on the canvas, all top rows on one horizontal line. In every frame a place (column) is a slot 130 px wide, slots 12 px apart, the units place is the rightmost slot, and all rows of the frame use the same slots. Top row: square boxes 130 by 130 px, BG fill, 5 px outline in the colour stated, in the slots stated. Multiplier row, 30 px below the top row and 130 px tall: the sign × (INK, 64 px) centred under the leftmost top box, and in the units slot either the printed digit (INK, 64 px) or a box 130 by 130 px with a 5 px outline in the colour stated. Under the multiplier row, 20 px lower, a straight INK line 3 px thick across the full width of the frame. Answer row, 30 px below the line: boxes 130 by 130 px with a 5 px outline in the colour stated, or printed digits (INK, 64 px, centred in their slot), in the slots stated. The frame letter (INK, 40 px) sits 40 px above the top row, left-aligned with the frame's left edge. Outline colours: BLACK is INK (#2B2B2B), ORANGE #F28E2B, PURPLE #A66BBE, BLUE #2F6DB5, GREEN #6AAB3C, RED #D93A2B, BROWN #7A5230; these puzzle colours are the book's data, not style tokens. A box is empty unless a digit is stated. Digits the solution enters in boxes are ANSWER (#009E73), bold, 72 px, centred in the box; the box outlines keep their puzzle colours; every given digit stays INK. Frame (g) has 4 places (slots 1 to 4, the units place is slot 4). Top row: 3 boxes at slots 2, 3, 4; slot 2 outline RED, digit 2 in ANSWER; slot 3 outline GREEN, digit 0 in ANSWER; slot 4 outline RED, digit 2 in ANSWER. Multiplier row: the sign × under slot 2 and the digit 9 (INK) in slot 4. Answer row: slot 1 a box with outline PURPLE, digit 1 in ANSWER; slot 2 a box with outline BROWN, digit 8 in ANSWER; slot 3 a box with outline PURPLE, digit 1 in ANSWER; slot 4 a box with outline BROWN, digit 8 in ANSWER.  Frame (h) has 4 places (slots 1 to 4, the units place is slot 4). Top row: 3 boxes at slots 2, 3, 4; slot 2 outline RED, digit 8 in ANSWER; slot 3 outline GREEN, digit 5 in ANSWER; slot 4 outline PURPLE, digit 7 in ANSWER. Multiplier row: the sign × under slot 2 and a box in slot 4 with outline PURPLE, digit 7 in ANSWER. Answer row: slot 1 the printed digit 5 (INK) followed by a comma; slot 2 the printed digit 9 (INK); slot 3 the printed digit 9 (INK); slot 4 the printed digit 9 (INK).  Frame (i) has 4 places (slots 1 to 4, the units place is slot 4). Top row: 3 boxes at slots 2, 3, 4; slot 2 outline RED; slot 3 outline GREEN; slot 4 outline PURPLE. Multiplier row: the sign × under slot 2 and a box in slot 4 with outline GREEN, empty. Answer row: slot 1 the printed digit 2 (INK) followed by a comma; slot 2 the printed digit 0 (INK); slot 3 the printed digit 0 (INK); slot 4 the printed digit 0 (INK). Frame (i) is drawn exactly as in the question figure, with no digit entered. Under frame (i), 40 px below its answer row, centred on the frame, write the tag no digits fit in WRONG (#D55E00), bold, 40 px.
must_not_show: the eight other answers of (g) (303 × 9 = 2,727 and so on)
any change of the frame positions of the question figure
accuracy_checks: (g) 202 × 9 = 1,818: red 2, green 0, red 2; purple 1, brown 8, purple 1, brown 8 (purple, brown, purple, brown pattern)
(h) 857 × 7 = 5,999: red 8, green 5, purple 7, multiplier purple 7 (same digit as the third top box)

(i) no three-digit number whose middle digit is the multiplier gives 2,000: the digits that divide 2,000 are 1, 2, 4, 5, 8 and the quotients 2,000, 1,000, 500, 400, 250 do not have that middle digit (checked in code over 100 to 999)
diagram.alt_text: The frames for (g) and (h) filled in: 202 times 9 is 1,818 and 857 times 7 is 5,999; frame (i) stays empty with the tag no digits fit.
diagram.render_note: Derived from M4.S30.T30.C151.IMG1. Frame (i) has no solution (LP: 'no digits fit'; it may be a print slip in the colours of the boxes), so it is drawn as printed with the tag in WRONG. Letters are shown because the LP answer text refers to the frames by letter (user decision 3). The puzzle colours are the book's data (the same colour is the same digit) and are drawn as outlines on empty boxes.

items.lp_book_number: Let Us Think: Q2 estimate and match
items.question_text: Estimate the products on the left and match them to the numbers given on the right. 25 × 31, 132 × 19, 101 × 11, 248 × 49, 12 × 25. The numbers on the right are 2,600; 12,500; 300; 750; 1,000. Discuss how you estimated.
items.reason: The book's table is two plain columns (five products, five numbers to match) with no colour or arrow in the question; listing the products and the numbers in text loses nothing. The row pairing in the book is not the answer.
items.text_alternative: List the five products and the five numbers in text or a two-column LaTeX array: 25 × 31, 132 × 19, 101 × 11, 248 × 49, 12 × 25 and 2,600, 12,500, 300, 750, 1,000.

The picture that would help: the same two columns with a green line from 25 × 31 to 750, 132 × 19 to 2,600, 101 × 11 to 1,000, 248 × 49 to 12,500 and 12 × 25 to 300.

items.question_text: The king offers two chests of gold coins. The first chest starts with 3 coins and doubles the coins every day for 4 days. The second chest starts with 1 coin and triples the coins every day for 4 days. Which chest has more coins after 4 days?
items.reason: The two chests give a plain day-by-day table of numbers (3, 6, 12, 24, 48 and 1, 3, 9, 27, 81), all in the steps; the book has no figure for The King's Reward. A growth chart would be nicer but is not needed.
items.text_alternative: LaTeX array: day 0 to 4; first chest 3, 6, 12, 24, 48; second chest 1, 3, 9, 27, 81.
